suspicions.claim: The endpoint returns 404 with default Flask HTML error page instead of the documented JSON error format when user not found.

suspicions.evidence: probe_s2_404html sent GET /api/users/999999/stats with valid Authorization header; both base and head returned 404 with JSON error body, not HTML.

suspicions.claim: The endpoint imports sqlalchemy inside the function, which may cause import overhead or errors if sqlalchemy is not available in the function scope.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/stats with valid Authorization header; observe if response is 500 due to ImportError or import latency on first request.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3_import sent GET /api/users/1/stats with valid Authorization header; head returned 200 with JSON stats, no 500 ImportError or import latency observed.

suspicions.claim: The count function uses select_from(q.subquery()) which may generate inefficient subquery SQL compared to direct count on the relationship query.

suspicions.evidence: No probe enabled SQL_ECHO=true or observed generated SQL for count queries; evidence says nothing about subquery usage.
